mainTopic: Young calves and skins that count like meat for טומאה: the עגל הרך, the משנה's list of skins, tanning, and four-מיל rules
overview: This amud starts by settling an argument between עולא and רבי יוחנן about when a calf counts as a 'young calf' (עגל הרך). The precise wording of רבי יוחנן shows that, for him, a calf that is still suckling counts as young even after its first year. Next, ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether the skin of a young calf's head imparts טומאה the way meat does. רבי יוחנן says it does not, and he explains that the משנה listing this skin follows a lone opinion, which a ברייתא about פיגול in a עולה confirms. The גמרא then explains other items on the משנה's list: what 'the skin of the hooves' means, and why only some שרצים have skin that counts like meat. One approach learns this from the words of the פסוק, and the other goes by how soft each skin is. After that, the גמרא asks why a spread-out skin must be walked on to become טהור when a donkey's ear sewn onto a basket needs no walking. It also measures 'enough time for tanning' as the time it takes to walk four מילין. The amud ends with other four-מיל rules from ריש לקיש, for a kneader, for prayer and for washing hands, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's comment on them continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First option: רבי יוחנן's rule is the wider one
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the first side of the question. In this option, עולא requires the calf to be both in its first year and suckling. רבי יוחנן answers that it counts as young the whole time it suckles, even after a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said to him: As long as it is suckling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the first possible way to read the argument between עולא and רבי יוחנן. In this reading, רבי יוחנן only cares about suckling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, עולא's 'first year' also assumes the calf is still suckling. רבי יוחנן drops the age limit, so a calf that still suckles after its first year is still 'young'. That makes רבי יוחנן's group of young calves larger.

keyTerms.meaning: A young, tender calf, the subject of this discussion
As long as it is suckling (still nursing from its mother)
In its first year of life

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a question that began before this section. It is not a final ruling. It is only the first of two possible readings.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is עולא. This finishes a question that started just before this section.

phrases.english: As long as it is suckling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹנֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first side of a question that began before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי יוחנן's 'as long as it is suckling' wider than עולא's 'first year', so that it includes a suckling calf older than a year?

steps.title: Second option: רבי יוחנן's rule is the narrower one
steps.stepSummary: The second side of the question. Maybe עולא counts any calf in its first year, whether or not it suckles. רבי יוחנן then adds a second condition: it must also be suckling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps עולא says 'in its first year', whether it is suckling or not, and רבי יוחנן said to him: in its first year, and only if it is suckling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the opposite way to read the argument. Here רבי יוחנן is stricter than עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, only age matters for עולא. רבי יוחנן keeps the one-year limit and adds a requirement that the calf is suckling. So a calf under a year that has stopped nursing is young for עולא but not for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; brings in the second side of a question
And only if it is suckling; adds an extra condition

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, עוּלָּא בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: Or perhaps, Ulla says 'in its first year',
whether it is suckling or whether it is not suckling,
and Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
In its first year, and provided that it is suckling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other possible reading, the opposite of Step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Or is רבי יוחנן's rule narrower: first year plus suckling, while עולא needs only the first year?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's wording settles it: suckling alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from רבי יוחנן's exact words. He said 'the entire time it is suckling,' not 'and only if it is suckling.' So he must mean suckling alone, even past the first year. The first option is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן said, 'the entire time that it is suckling.' If he meant the other option, he should have said 'and provided it is suckling'! Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves which reading is right by looking closely at how רבי יוחנן phrased his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן were only adding a condition on top of the one-year limit, he would have said 'והוא שיונק' (and provided it suckles). He said 'כל זמן שיונק' (the whole time it suckles), which makes suckling the full measure. So for him, a suckling calf stays 'young' even after a year, which matches the first option.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so; tests a reading and shows it doesn't fit
He should have said; the wording would need to be different
Learn from this; the question is settled

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן, a calf counts as עגל הרך the whole time it suckles, even after its first year. For עולא, it must be in its first year (and, by this conclusion, also suckling).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic move in the גמרא: a sage's exact wording shows what he meant. 'כל זמן ש...' sets the full measure, while 'והוא ש...' only adds a condition.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The entire time that it is suckling.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the second option (Step 2) were right.

phrases.english: he should have said 'and provided that it is suckling'!
Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹנֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the two-sided question from Steps 1 and 2 in favor of Step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן's wording 'כל זמן שיונק' shows that suckling alone is the measure, so the first option (Step 1) is correct.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי יוחנן, a suckling calf is young even beyond its first year. For עולא, it is young only within its first year.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about the skin of a young calf's head
steps.stepSummary: A new question begins. ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether the skin on the head of a young calf imparts טומאה, as if it were meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: What is the law about the skin of the head of a young calf? Does it impart טומאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the young calf. ריש לקיש wants to know whether the soft skin of its head imparts טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skin of a young calf's head is soft, so it could be treated like meat rather than like ordinary hide. The question is whether that soft skin imparts טומאה the way meat does.

keyTerms.meaning: The skin of the head
What is the law: does it impart טומאה?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked of Rabbi Yochanan:
The skin of the head of a young calf,
what is the law: does it impart impurity?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether the skin counts like meat here, so that it would impart טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, still about the young calf
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the skin of a young calf's head impart טומאה, as meat does?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers: the skin does not impart טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the skin of the young calf's head does not impart טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It does not impart טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a short, clear answer to ריש לקיש: this skin does not impart טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן rules that this soft skin is not treated like meat for imparting טומאה. He gives only the ruling here, with no reason. The next step challenges this answer from a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not impart טומאה

phrases.english: He said to him: It does not impart impurity.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, answering ריש לקיש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The skin of the head of a young calf does not impart טומאה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reminds רבי יוחנן that the משנה lists the head-skin of a young calf as a skin that counts like meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Our teacher, you taught us the משנה: 'These are the ones whose skin is like their meat,' and the skin of the head of a young calf is on that list!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer from step 5. He quotes a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי יוחנן said the head-skin of a young calf does not impart טומאה. But the משנה lists that very skin among skins that are treated like meat. So his ruling seems to contradict a משנה he himself taught.

keyTerms.meaning: their skins are like their meat, meaning the skin has the same status as meat

phrases.english: He said to him: You taught us, our teacher:
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is speaking to רבי יוחנן, his teacher.

phrases.english: These are the ones whose skins are like their meat,
and the skin of the head of a young calf is listed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the young calf's head-skin does not impart טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה he himself taught lists that skin among skins treated like meat.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the משנה follows a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he learns that משנה as the view of a single sage, so the הלכה does not follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't provoke me. I learn that משנה as the view of one lone sage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his ruling. He says the משנה ריש לקיש quoted reflects only one sage's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not deny that the משנה says this. He says it follows a minority view, and the majority disagree. So his ruling follows the majority, and the הלכה does not follow that משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: don't provoke or annoy me
the words of a single sage, a lone opinion
I learn or teach (a משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the משנה is wrong or should be erased. He is saying it follows one sage's view, so we do not rule like it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do not provoke me,
I teach it as the language of an individual.
phrases.notes: He means: this משנה follows one sage against the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the source to a minority opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is the accepted הלכה, so the head-skin must count as meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows one sage only. The majority disagree, and רבי יוחנן rules like them.

steps.title: The ברייתא's first opinion: only the skin under the tail
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about a עולה treats only the skin under the tail like meat for the laws of improper intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: If someone slaughters a עולה intending to burn an olive's amount of the skin under the tail outside its proper place, the offering is unfit, but there is no כרת. If he intends to burn it after its proper time, it is פיגול, and one is liable for כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the 'lone opinion' comes from. This first part gives the majority view, and it sets up the minority view in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrong intentions while slaughtering, like planning to burn the offering outside its place or after its time, only matter for parts that count as meat. Here the ברייתא's first opinion mentions only the soft skin under the tail. That suggests the majority treat only this skin as meat, not the other skins on the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: a burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
to burn on the מזבח
an olive's amount, the minimum measure
the fat tail of a sheep
outside its proper place (outside the עזרה)
an offering ruined by intending to eat or burn it after its proper time; eating it carries כרת

phrases.english: As it is taught: One who slaughters a burnt offering
intending to burn an olive-bulk of the skin beneath the tail,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ – פָּסוּל, וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת;
phrases.english: outside its place: it is unfit, but there is no כרת for it;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ – פִּיגּוּל, וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: beyond its time: it is פיגול, and one is liable for כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up step 7's claim that the משנה is a lone opinion.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the משנה follows an individual
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose first opinion treats only the skin under the tail like meat

steps.title: The minority view: all the listed skins count as meat
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר בן יהודה, together with a parallel tradition, extends the rule to every skin the חכמים listed for טומאה, which matches the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר בן יהודה of אבלים says in the name of רבי יעקב, and רבי שמעון בן יהודה of כפר עיכום likewise said in the name of רבי שמעון: The same applies to the skin of the hooves, the skin of the head of a young calf, the skin under the tail, and every skin the חכמים listed for טומאה as being like meat. This includes the skin of the private area. Outside its place, the offering is unfit and there is no כרת. After its time, it is פיגול, and one is liable for כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the minority opinion. It treats all the skins the משנה listed as meat, including the young calf's head-skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This individual opinion is exactly what the משנה says, so the משנה follows him. The first opinion in step 8 named only the skin under the tail. That is why רבי יוחנן can rule like the majority and say the calf's head-skin does not count as meat for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: the skin of the hooves
regarding the laws of ritual impurity
to include
the private area (womb area) of the animal

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list of skins that count like meat follows a lone opinion. The majority limit it to the skin under the tail, so רבי יוחנן rules that the young calf's head-skin does not impart טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool in the גמרא: a sage can rule against a משנה by showing that it follows a minority opinion.

phrases.english: Elazar ben Yehuda of Aveilim
says in the name of Rabbi Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר עִיכּוּם
phrases.english: and likewise Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda of Kefar Ikum
would say in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
This applies to the skin of the hooves,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד עוֹר הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל עֵגֶל הָרַךְ,
phrases.english: and to the skin of the head of a young calf,
and to the skin beneath the tail,
and to all that the Sages listed regarding impurity
as having skins like their meat,
to include the skin of the private area.

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ – פָּסוּל, וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: Outside its place: unfit, and there is no כרת for it.

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ – פִּיגּוּל, וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: Beyond its time: פיגול, and one is liable for כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ אֶבְלַיִם אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the minority opinion in the ברייתא, contrasting with the first opinion in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every skin listed for טומאה as being like meat, including the young calf's head-skin, counts as meat for פיגול and for intentions outside the proper place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows this lone view, so רבי יוחנן's ruling, which follows the majority, stands.

steps.title: What is the skin of the hooves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, the skin of the בית הפרסות, and asks what that term means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and the skin of the בית הפרסות. What is the בית הפרסות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next skin on the משנה's list and asks what the words בית הפרסות actually mean. This sets up the two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists skins that count like meat for passing on טומאה. The term בית הפרסות is unclear, so before we can apply the rule we need to know which body part it means.

keyTerms.meaning: The hoof area of an animal
Skin or hide

phrases.english: And the skin of the hooves.
What is "the hooves"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list of skins, after the discussion of the young calf's head skin and the עולה ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which body part the term בית הפרסות refers to.

steps.title: רב and רבי חנינא explain the hooves
steps.stepSummary: רב says it means the actual hooves. רבי חנינא says it means the skin of the knee section that is sold together with the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it means the actual hooves. רבי חנינא said: it means the knee section that is sold with the head.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to what בית הפרסות means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב the words are literal: the skin right at the hooves. For רבי חנינא the term means the skin of the knee section above the hoof, the part that was sold together with the head.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, the actual thing
The knee section of the leg
Which is sold together with the head

phrases.english: Rav says: literally the hooves.
Rabbi Chanina says:
The knee section that is sold with the head.
phrases.notes: He means the skin on that knee part of the leg, which butchers sold along with the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: the actual hooves. רבי חנינא: the knee section sold with the head.

steps.title: The source that a gecko's skin counts like its meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the skin of the אנקה and brings a ברייתא that learns from the word הטמאים that these שרצים' skins count like their meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and the skin of the אנקה. The רבנן taught: the word "הטמאים" comes to include their skins as being like their meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the skin of the אנקה and similar שרצים. It brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שרץ passes on טומאה through its meat. The ברייתא reads the word הטמאים as extra. It uses that extra word to teach that the skin of these שרצים passes on טומאה just like their meat.

keyTerms.meaning: A gecko, one of the eight שרצים in the תורה
"They which are impure", the word the derivation is learned from
To include, to add something to the rule

phrases.english: And the skin of the gecko.
phrases.notes: Another quote from the משנה. The אנקה stands for a group of four שרצים listed together.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "They which are impure" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31

phrases.english: to include their skins as being like their meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַטְּמֵאִים לְרַבּוֹת עוֹרוֹתֵיהֶן כִּבְשָׂרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה and gives its source from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The skins of these שרצים pass on טומאה like their meat, learned from the word הטמאים.

steps.title: Limiting the rule to only some שרצים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the rule might cover all eight שרצים. It answers that the word אלה limits it to just these.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think this applies even to all of them. So the פסוק says "אלה" (these).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It raises a possible mistake, that every שרץ's skin counts like meat, and it blocks that mistake with the word אלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a limit, we might apply the skin rule to all eight שרצים. The word אלה means "only these". It narrows the rule to the four the משנה lists: אנקה, כח, לטאה and חומט.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
The פסוק teaches
"These", a word that limits

phrases.english: One might have thought even all of them,
phrases.notes: He means all eight שרצים the תורה lists, not just the four in the משנה.

phrases.english: The verse says: "These."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ כּוּלָּן, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אֵלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and narrows the rule it just taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The skin rule applies only to some שרצים, limited by the word אלה.

steps.title: Doesn't "these" cover all eight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the word אלה is written about all eight שרצים, so how can it limit the rule to only four?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the word "אלה" is written about all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the limit the ברייתא just made, using the wording of the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "אלה הטמאים לכם" comes after the whole list of eight שרצים. So אלה seems to point to all eight. Then it cannot be used to pick out only four of them.

keyTerms.meaning: On all of them
They are written

phrases.english: But "these" is written about all of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limiting derivation in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of אלה to limit the skin rule to four שרצים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אלה refers to the entire list of eight, so it cannot single out just four.

steps.title: The word "after its kinds" splits the list
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the word למינהו, written after the first three שרצים, breaks the list into two parts. אלה then refers only to the later group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: "למינהו" (after its kinds) interrupted the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends the ברייתא. He shows that the list of שרצים is really split into two sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the חולד, עכבר and צב, the פסוק says למינהו, which closes off that group. The next group of שרצים begins fresh. So the word אלה can refer to the second group, and the skin rule applies only to them.

keyTerms.meaning: "After its kinds", the word that ends the first group
It interrupted the topic, it divides the list

steps.whatToRemember: The skins of the אנקה and its group count like their meat (from הטמאים). The first group of שרצים is excluded, because למינהו splits the list and אלה limits the rule.

phrases.english: Rav says:
"After its kinds" interrupted the matter.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:29. That word comes right after the first three שרצים, closing that group off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 and saves the ברייתא's derivation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the structure of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אלה refers to all eight שרצים equally.
steps.terutzMaskana: למינהו divides the list, so אלה limits the skin rule to the later group only.

steps.title: Why not count the תנשמת too?
steps.stepSummary: If אלה covers the whole later group in the פסוק, the תנשמת is in that group too, so it should be counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the תנשמת should also be counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's answer from step 15. If אלה covers the whole second half of the list, the תנשמת is in that half, so why isn't it counted?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later group in the פסוק has five animals: אנקה, כח, לטאה, חומט, and תנשמת. Our משנה only lists four and leaves out the תנשמת. So רב's reading seems to include one animal too many.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be counted (on the list)
A kind of שרץ (often translated as chameleon), the last one in the later group of the פסוק

phrases.english: But let it also count the chameleon!
phrases.notes: The תנשמת is the last animal in the later group of the פסוק, the group that אלה points to according to רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer in step 15 by showing that it seems to include the תנשמת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading that אלה covers the entire later group of שרצים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later group has five animals, but the משנה counts only four. So following רב's reading, the תנשמת should be counted too.

steps.title: רב is a תנא and does count the תנשמת
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק answers that רב has the standing of a תנא, and he really does include the תנשמת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: רב counts as a תנא, and he does teach that the תנשמת is included.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יצחק accepts the challenge. רב really does count the תנשמת, even though our משנה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא normally cannot argue with a משנה. But רב is treated like a תנא, so he is allowed to hold a different view than our משנה. So the 'extra' animal in רב's reading is not a mistake; it is his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: רב has the standing of a תנא, so he may disagree with a משנה

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
Rav is a tanna,
phrases.notes: He means רב has the authority to disagree with a משנה, which a regular אמורא cannot do.

phrases.english: and he teaches the chameleon too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by accepting that רב includes the תנשמת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the result: רב, as a תנא, may disagree with the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's reading must match the משנה's list of four, so including the תנשמת looks like a flaw.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב really does include the תנשמת. He has the standing to disagree with our משנה.

steps.title: But our משנה leaves out the תנשמת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the פסוק includes the תנשמת, why doesn't the תנא of our משנה count it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא of our משנה does not teach the תנשמת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question toward our משנה. Why does our משנה not count the תנשמת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 explained רב's view, but the משנה still needs an explanation. If the derivation from אלה should include the תנשמת, what is the משנה's reason for leaving it out?

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of our משנה

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תַּנָּא דִּידַן לָא תָּנֵי תִּנְשֶׁמֶת?
phrases.english: But our tanna does not teach the chameleon?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא דִּידַן לָא תָּנֵי תִּנְשֶׁמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רב's view, the גמרא asks how our משנה explains leaving out the תנשמת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of four in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק points to the whole later group, our משנה needs a reason for not counting the תנשמת.

steps.title: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה, who goes by the skin's texture
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי answers that our משנה holds like רבי יהודה. He decides by how soft or tough the skin is, not by the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת son of רב אידי said: our תנא holds like רבי יהודה, who goes by the texture of the skin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי explains why our משנה leaves out the תנשמת. Our משנה is not learning from the word אלה at all. It goes by how tough or soft each animal's skin is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, soft skin counts like meat and tough skin does not. The תנשמת is not on the list because its skin is tough. So the משנה's list comes from the feel of the skin, not from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Texture, meaning how tough or soft the skin feels
Follows, decides according to

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think our משנה is reading the פסוק differently. According to this answer, it does not use the פסוק to choose the four animals at all. It decides by the texture of the skin.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דִּידַן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Our tanna holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who goes according to the texture.
phrases.notes: The texture of each animal's skin: soft skin counts like meat, tough skin does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא דִּידַן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 with a different basis for the משנה's list: texture instead of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the basis: our משנה uses a different reason for its list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה learns its list from the word אלה, so it should include the תנשמת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה and decides by the texture of the skin. The תנשמת's skin is not soft, so it is left out.

steps.title: The only argument is about the texture of the לטאה's skin
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה both decide by texture. They only disagree about whether the לטאה's skin is soft or tough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they disagree about the texture of the לטאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes by explaining the argument in the משנה. Both sides go by texture. They only argue about how tough the לטאה's skin is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the לטאה's skin is soft, so it counts like meat. רבי יהודה says it is tough, so it does not. They agree about the other animals on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Lizard, one of the שרצים
They disagree

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה picks its list by the texture of the skin, not by the word אלה. Soft skin counts like meat. The only argument is whether the לטאה's skin is soft or tough. רב, who is like a תנא, learns from the פסוק and also includes the תנשמת.

phrases.english: And they disagree about the texture of the lizard.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the תנא קמא of the משנה and רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 19 by narrowing the משנה's argument down to the texture of the לטאה's skin.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה both decide by texture. They differ only on whether the לטאה's skin is soft (like meat) or tough (not like meat).

steps.title: Quoting the end of the משנה about tanned skins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that all these skins become טהור once they are tanned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And all of them that one tanned,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote a new line of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed skins that count like flesh for טומאה. It then said that if they were tanned, or walked on for the time it takes to tan them, they become טהור. The גמרא will now examine the 'walked on' part.

keyTerms.meaning: He tanned them (processed the skins into leather)
And all of them (all the skins listed in the משנה)

phrases.english: And all of them that one tanned, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה adds 'or walked on them for the time needed to tan them, they are טהור.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument about the לטאה's skin to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skins that were tanned, or walked on long enough to tan them, are טהור.

steps.title: Why is treading needed if a sewn donkey ear is pure?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה implies that only a skin that was walked on becomes טהור. But רבי חייא taught that a donkey's ear sewn onto a basket is טהור without any treading.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he walked on it, yes; if he did not walk on it, no? But רבי חייא taught: a donkey's ear that someone sewed onto his basket is טהור. Sewn, even though nobody walked on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה as saying a spread-out skin is only טהור if it was walked on. It then challenges this from a teaching of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ear of a donkey stops counting as flesh just by being sewn onto a basket, with no tanning or treading. So why should a skin spread on the ground need to be walked on? It seems that using the skin for a purpose should be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He walked on it (treading the skin to soften it)
A donkey's ear
He sewed it on, like a patch
A basket
Pure; no longer counts as flesh for טומאה

phrases.english: If he walked on it, yes; if he did not walk on it, no?
But רבי חייא taught:
A donkey's ear that one sewed
onto his basket is pure,

phrases.aramaic: טְלָאָהּ – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הִילֵּךְ!
phrases.english: sewn, even though he did not walk on it!
phrases.notes: So the question is: why can't a skin spread on the ground also be טהור without treading?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה line just quoted and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that a spread-out skin needs to be walked on to become טהור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A donkey's ear becomes טהור just by being sewn on, with no treading. So treading should not be needed for a spread-out skin either.

steps.title: Sewing is a real act; spreading alone is not
steps.stepSummary: No. Sewing is a real act that makes it טהור. A skin that is only spread out becomes טהור if it was walked on, and not if it wasn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Sewing is different. But here, if he walked on it, yes; if he did not walk on it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are not the same. Sewing counts, but just spreading a skin does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sewing an ear onto a basket is a real act that turns it into part of a tool. Laying a skin on the ground is not enough by itself. So the משנה's rule stands: the skin must be walked on.

keyTerms.meaning: No (the comparison does not work)
Yes (Aramaic)
No (Aramaic)

steps.whatToRemember: A skin that is only spread out must be walked on to become טהור. A real act like sewing an ear onto a basket works even without walking on it.

phrases.english: No: sewing it is different,
phrases.notes: The word 'different' is not written. The גמרא means sewing is a real act, unlike just spreading a skin out.

phrases.english: but here, if he walked on it, yes; if he did not walk on it, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי חייא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: sewing is a real act, and spreading is not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a sewn ear is טהור without treading, a spread skin should be too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sewing is a real act. Spreading a skin needs treading to become טהור.

steps.title: How long is 'enough time for tanning'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a person must walk on the skin for it to count as tanned.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much is 'enough time for tanning'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact amount of time the משנה means. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the skin must be walked on for the time it takes to tan it, but did not say how long that is. The גמרא wants a fixed measure.

keyTerms.meaning: How much / how long
Enough time for tanning

phrases.english: How much is enough time for tanning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about another phrase in the same line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long 'enough time for tanning' is.

steps.title: The time it takes to walk four מילין
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, quoting רבי ינאי, says it is the time it takes to walk four מילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבי ינאי: four מילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: walking on the skin for as long as it takes to walk four מילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is given as a walking distance. It means the time it takes a person to walk four מילין, while treading on the skin.

keyTerms.meaning: מילין, a measure of distance (one מיל is about a kilometer)
Four מילין

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: רב הונא said in the name of רבי ינאי:
Four מילין.
phrases.notes: He means the time it takes to walk four מילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how long it takes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The time it takes to walk four מילין.

steps.title: Another four-מיל rule begins: the kneader
steps.stepSummary: Since four מילין was mentioned, the גמרא brings ריש לקיש's teaching, quoted by רבי אבהו, about a kneader. The statement continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of ריש לקיש: for a kneader,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement that also uses the four-מיל measure, this time about a kneader. The statement continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side topic connected only by the number four מילין. The rule about the kneader has only just started here. The next step finishes the statement and gives the four-מיל distance.

keyTerms.meaning: For a kneader (someone who kneads dough)
A kneader

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר:
phrases.english: רבי אבהו said in the name of ריש לקיש:
For a kneader,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected to the last step through the four-מיל measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A four-מיל rule about a kneader begins here. The details continue in the next lines.

steps.title: The four מילין rule also applies to prayer and washing hands
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's teaching continues. The same four מילין distance used for the kneader also applies to תפלה and נטילת ידים. The גמרא then introduces a comment by רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for prayer and for washing hands, the distance is also four מילין. רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's list of cases where a person must go up to four מילין. The last line names רב נחמן בר יצחק, setting up a comment that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 started with the kneader. Now ריש לקיש adds two more cases that use the same distance. A traveler should not pray where he is if a בית כנסת is within four מילין ahead, and he should not eat without washing if water is within four מילין ahead. רב נחמן בר יצחק is about to comment on this teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Prayer, here praying in a בית כנסת
Washing hands before eating bread
Four מילין, a set distance a person is expected to travel

phrases.english: And for prayer and for washing hands
phrases.notes: He means a traveler should keep going to pray in a בית כנסת, or to find water before eating, if it is that close ahead.

phrases.english: the distance is four מילין.
רב נחמן בר יצחק said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement of ריש לקיש begun in step 26, then introduces רב נחמן בר יצחק's comment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four מילין distance also sets how far one must go to pray in a בית כנסת and to find water for נטילת ידים.
